title.narrative: Epifanio de los Santos Avenue Greenways Project

description.narrative: The project aims to improve pedestrian environment in four areas along with Epifanio Delos Santos Avenue (EDSA). The current pedestrian facilities on EDSA is poorly designed and pedestrians are suffered from the unsafe and uncomfortable pedestrian environment. The elevated walkways will be connected to railway stations and help promoting use of public transportation. The project will build a total of 5-kilometers (km) of elevated walkways in four areas, including the construction of new footbridges, replacement or widening of existing footbridges. The elevated walkways will be covered to protect pedestrians from sunlight and rains. Elevators will be attached to the elevated walkways to address the needs of the elderly, persons with disability (PWDs), and people traveling with small children.

ADB fielded a project midterm review mission on 23-24 November 2022 to review overall project progress and update the project’s contract awards and disbursement projections. DOTr will request for loan extension from the Government and once approved, will submit the same to ADB for review and approval.

DOTr submitted the updated bidding documents (BDs) for CP01 and CP02 for ADB review on 28 March 2023. ADB shared the comments on the BDs to DOTr for their action on 14 April 2023 and the revised BDs were submitted to ADB on 5 May 2023. ADB issued no objection to the BDs on 17 May 2023 but no final invitation for bids (IFBs) are received to date. As per DOTr's latest advice in their 2nd quarter 2023 progress report, the IFB publication is in July 2023.
The recruitment of the construction supervision consultant has commenced. The CSRN was published on 30 December 2021. Sixteen (16) expressions of interest (EOIs) were received by the EOI submission deadline date of 28 January 2022. ADB reviewed the Submission 1 and shared the comments with the EA on 21 November 2022. No revised Submission 1 has been received yet.
On 23 September 2021, ADB approved a minor change allowing DOTr to delegate to the Department of Budget and Management Procurement Service (DBM-PS) the procurement of civil works contract and recruitment of the construction supervision consultant. As a procuring agent, DBM-PS will undertake procurement activities on behalf of DOTr who remains the procuring entity and responsible for contract implementation. The MOA between DOTr and PS-DBM was terminated in September 2022 and so all unadvertised contract packages and procurement responsibilities reverted to DOTr.
